subject: platform/billing
professional: a senior payments engineer who has integrated Stripe and Paddle Billing webhooks and shipped signed licence keys; first checks: is Paddle-Signature verified over the raw body with a constant-time compare and a timestamp window, are replayed and out-of-order deliveries idempotent, does the product come from the paid price not client data, do subscription keys follow the paid period, is the signing scheme sound, and what happens when a buyer pays and does not get or loses the key

evidence.correctness: Recomputed against sources the author did not write. (1) Took Paddle's own transaction.completed example payload from developer.paddle.com/webhooks/transactions/transaction-completed (reachable today), set custom_data.claim, pretty-printed it as the raw body, computed h1 with `openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac <secret>` over `ts:body` per Paddle's 'Verify webhook signatures' page, and posted it to handleBilling (scratch recompute.mjs): 200 and a key stored; one-byte tamper 401; the same JSON re-serialised compactly 401 (raw body is what is signed); uppercase hex 200; two h1 (rotation) 200; ts+301 401. (2) The key's exp for that payload: billing_period.ends_at 2024-05-12T10:18:47.635628Z floored + 7*86400, computed in Python datetime = 1716113927; observed claims.exp 1716113927, s = the payload's sub_01hv8x29kz0t586xy6zn1a62ny, p from the price id (items[].price.id; Paddle's webhook items carry price.id, not price_id, and the code reads both). (3) The Ed25519 signature on the minted key verified with `openssl pkeyutl -verify -rawin` over `ms1.<payload>`: 'Signature Verified Successfully'; 64-byte signature, 32-byte public key. (4) d1Store's SQL run against schema.sql in node:sqlite: out-of-order renewal (exp 200 then 100) keeps 200, newer 300 replaces, a replayed claim keeps the first key. One departure: tolerance 300 s where Paddle's SDKs and docs use 5 s (a ts+6 delivery is accepted here, refused by @paddle/paddle-node-sdk 3.12.0 WebhooksValidator); harmless in effect because every write is idempotent.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked: Paddle-Signature check (works, above); Ed25519 ms1 key (works); stored under SHA-256(claim), not the code (claimHash prefixes 'ms-billing-claim:'; works); product from price, never custom_data (test 'the product comes from the paid price' and my run: custom_data.product ignored); retry keeps the first key and ignored events answer 200 (works); subscription expiry a week after the period and POST /billing/renew (works, billing.test.mjs renew test and sqlite store); sync.mjs copies client.mjs to 7 ventures (`node platform/billing/sync.mjs --check`: 'billing copies in sync'); edge Worker does not mount /billing and no Actions deploy (tested). Dark by design until the owner's Going-live steps; nothing is a stub. Not done and said so: Paddle catalogue as code, quick-pick-survey pack.
evidence.verification: `node --test billing.test.mjs` (Node 22.23.5): 19 tests, 19 pass, 0.43 s; ventures/wall-framing-takeoff licence.test.mjs + checkout.test.mjs 3 pass. CI: ventures-tests.yml triggers on platform/** and runs this suite. Seeded 9 mutants with quality_mutate.py: tolerance x1000, grace removed, renew <= -> <, D1 upsert WHERE dropped, claim DO NOTHING -> DO UPDATE, status check removed, expiry +1 day, size cap removed all caught (8/9); worker.mjs CORS reflecting any origin survived. Tests run the real SQL against the real schema. No test of the browser wireBuy persistence ordering (defect 2).
evidence.craft: Read worker.mjs, server.mjs, client.mjs, catalogue.mjs, sync.mjs, keygen.mjs, schema.sql, testkit.mjs, billing.test.mjs whole. Small, dependency-free WebCrypto code; ids validated by pattern; constant-time compare equivalent to Paddle's SDK; JSON responses no-store. Minor: MAX_WEBHOOK_BYTES compares raw.length (UTF-16 units) after the whole body is read, so it bounds nothing on the wire; worker CORS falls back to origins[0] for a foreign origin (harmless, untested); sameString leaks length only (fine, fixed-length hex).
evidence.claims: README 'How a sale works', 'Files', guardrail section and the honest 'What is not verified' section are backed by files and tests. Two drifts: keygen.mjs:8 tells the owner to `wrangler secret put LICENCE_SIGNING_KEY (in platform/edge/)`, which contradicts README step 1 and worker.mjs (billing account, never the public edge Worker) on the one step that places a secret; README:123 says Paddle's docs host does not resolve and the field names are from memory: today it resolves and every field used matches the docs example (status, items[].price.id, custom_data, subscription_id, billing_period.ends_at), so the caveat is stale in the safe direction.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job end to end in simulation: webhook from Paddle's example payload -> key minted -> GET /billing/claim returns it -> key verifies offline -> lapsed subscription key renews. The owner can go live with the README's steps. What a payments engineer would hit in the first week of support: (a) the claim code is persisted to localStorage only when Paddle.js fires checkout.completed (client.mjs:180), so a tab closed or crashed between payment and that event leaves a paid buyer with no way to collect the key; (b) after a key is fetched the claim is deleted (client.mjs:153) and the DB is keyed only by claim hash, with no index by Paddle transaction or subscription id, so a buyer who loses the key and writes in with their Paddle receipt cannot be reissued one without hand-decoding every row; there is no reissue tool.
evidence.domain: Compared with Paddle Billing's 'Verify webhook signatures' docs and @paddle/paddle-node-sdk 3.12.0 (dist/cjs/notifications/helpers/webhooks-validator.js): same HMAC-SHA256 over `ts:rawBody`, same constant-time compare, abs time difference; this code additionally accepts several h1 during secret rotation, which the SDK does not. Departure: 300 s window (Stripe's default) vs Paddle's 5 s; mitigated because claim writes are DO NOTHING and sub writes keep the max exp. Idempotency, out-of-order handling, price-derived entitlement and offline Ed25519 keys are what a practitioner would do. Refunds/chargebacks do not revoke (documented for one-off; for subscriptions the key runs to period end + 7 days, not stated).

defects.what: The claim code is written to localStorage only inside the checkout.completed callback, after payment; a tab closed, crashed or navigated away between Paddle charging and that event leaves a paid buyer with no claim and no way to collect the key (the server has it, nobody can ask). Persist the claim before Checkout.open.

No lost-key recovery: the claim is deleted once the key is fetched and licences are keyed only by claim hash, with no column or index by Paddle transaction/subscription id, so support cannot reissue a key from the buyer's Paddle receipt; no reissue script exists.

keygen.mjs tells the owner to set LICENCE_SIGNING_KEY '(in platform/edge/)', the public site's Worker, contradicting README step 1, worker.mjs and the Payments guardrail on the one step that places the signing secret.

Timestamp tolerance is 300 s; Paddle's docs and SDKs use 5 s. Replays inside the window are harmless because writes are idempotent, but it departs from the provider's documented default without saying why.
README 'What is not verified' says Paddle's docs host does not resolve and field names are from memory; it resolves now and the fields match the docs example payload, so the caveat is stale.
MAX_WEBHOOK_BYTES is checked as raw.length (UTF-16 code units) after the full body is read, so it neither counts bytes nor bounds what is read.
Worker CORS behaviour is untested: a mutant reflecting any Origin survived the suite (low impact, reads need a 128-bit claim).

verdict: A sound, small Paddle licence path. Recomputed with Paddle's own example payload signed by openssl, Python date arithmetic and openssl Ed25519 verification, every output matched: raw-body HMAC, rotation, tamper and window refusals, price-derived product, expiry = period end + 7 days, idempotent and order-safe D1 writes. Tests are strong (19 pass, 8 of 9 seeded mutants caught, real SQL against the real schema). It meets the bar on correctness, claims and verification. What keeps fitness at 2 is the support path a payments engineer worries about first: a buyer who loses the tab before checkout.completed, or later loses the key, has no recovery, and the store cannot look a key up by Paddle transaction id. One wrong instruction on the secret path (keygen.mjs says platform/edge) should be fixed before the owner runs keygen.
